# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Tuesday, November 24, 2026

Tuesday edition for 24 November 2026 (IST), covering Monday 23 November to Tuesday morning. **The equity, equity-derivative, currency and bond markets are closed today for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev (Guru Nanak Jayanti)**, so every index and stock figure below is Monday 23 November's close and there is no 24 November session to look for. IBJA's own block reads "Holiday", so its benchmark stays on Monday's PM session. This edition is published late: the 07:00 run could not reach the phone exit route, which had been offline since 23:54 the previous night, and the fetch was rebuilt at 07:27 IST once the phone reconnected — the source status is recorded at the end.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### RBI presses NBFCs on gold-loan LTVs as collateral falls, ET reports
The Reserve Bank of India met the managing directors and chief executives of select NBFCs, including government NBFCs, housing finance companies and microfinance institutions, in Mumbai on Monday 23 November, and the official readout is now out. RBI press release 2026-2027/1554, dated 23 November and signed by Brij Raj, Chief General Manager, records that representatives of Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC also participated, that **all four Deputy Governors — Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S. C. Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain** — attended with other senior officers, and that the **Managing Director and Chief Executive of the National Housing Bank also participated**.

The part that matters to a gold lender is not in the release. The Economic Times reported on Tuesday 24 November (01:11 IST) that the RBI "told non-banking finance companies about the need for greater scrutiny in their gold loans given falling gold prices that skew unfavourably for lenders' loan to value ratios", adding that gold has fallen close to 30% from its peak "in the last month or so, which means that outstanding value for some loans may have shrunk below the 85% loan to value ratio that the central bank stipulates for loans against gold."

ET quotes a person aware of the discussions that the meeting ran one and a half hours, and that "with gold prices down 35% to 40% and some of the companies close to 75% in terms of loan to value … The RBI said that companies must be more cautious. NBFCs were told that growth has been good so far but were cautioned against growing too quickly." The same report says NBFCs that fail to reach a ₹10 crore net owned fund by March 2027 will get no further extension, and that the RBI wanted greater scrutiny when onboarding new technology partners.

Moneycontrol reported the monitoring side on Monday (23 Nov, 10:04 IST): the RBI "has started increasing its portfolio monitoring over the last 30–45 days" and "has been asking all large NBFCs to report their portfolio numbers at a higher frequency compared to a monthly assessment." A senior executive at a gold loan company, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that "around 18 months back, when gold prices were at their all-time high, LTV was comfortably within the 70-80 percent level. Now with the steep correction that has happened, there are certain cases where LTV is seen breaching even 100 percent."

Two numbers put the scale on it. TransUnion CIBIL, cited by ET, has gold-loan NPAs at **0.30% at the end of August 2026 against 0.16% at 31 March 2026**. Moneycontrol, citing RBI data, puts loans against gold at **₹3.74 trillion in September 2026, up 66.1% year-on-year**.

The industry's response is a representation, not a change: the newly formed Federation of Gold Loan Companies, whose members include Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance, has asked the RBI to review the Tier-1 capital requirement so it aligns with other NBFCs, and to bring gold loans back into priority-sector lending.

Nothing here is a rule change. The RBI released no instrument on gold-loan LTV; the 85%/80%/75% ceilings and the 30-day-average valuation rule already stand in the June 2025 Directions. No lender has been named as breaching, and no company has been named as under supervisory action.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the reported scrutiny is sector-wide and no Muthoot Fincorp-specific detail appears in the sources checked. Its own last published asset-quality number is Stage III at 1.07% as at 30 September 2026, filed on 14 November, which is a lagging indicator against a price fall that mostly happened in October and November. The operative sentence for planning is the one about continuous LTV: the June 2025 Directions require the prescribed LTV to be maintained throughout the tenor, and the collateral is valued at the lower of a 30-day average and the previous day's close, which is why a fall reaches the book with a lag rather than on the day it happens.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1554, 23 Nov](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64032) · [Economic Times, 24 Nov 01:11 IST](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/rbi-cautions-nbfcs-over-falling-gold-prices-and-rising-loan-to-value-ratios/articleshow/136113465.cms) · [Moneycontrol, 23 Nov 10:04 IST](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/commodities/rbi-steps-up-monitoring-of-gold-loan-portfolios-of-banks-nbfcs-as-ltv-concerns-emerge-14086885.html)

### Gold rebounds 3.9% on Comex — its biggest one-day gain since August
Comex front-month gold **settled at $3,649.20 an ounce on Monday 23 November, up $136.90 or 3.90%** — the largest one-day dollar gain since 5 August 2026, the largest one-day percentage gain since 3 February 2026, and enough to snap a three-session losing streak. It is 3.90% above the 52-week low of $3,512.30 set on Friday 20 November, and still **down 15.64% year-to-date** (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 23 Nov, 18:52 ET).

Silver moved further: Comex front-month **settled at $43.147 an ounce, up $2.1120 or 5.15%**, the largest one-day percentage gain since 12 June 2026 and the largest dollar gain since 4 November 2026, also snapping a three-session losing streak and 5.15% above its own 52-week low of $41.035 set on 20 November (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 23 Nov, 18:53 ET).

On the domestic exchange, MCX's **GOLD 04DEC2026 contract last traded at ₹1,26,021 per 10 g, up ₹4,243 or 3.48%** against a previous close of ₹1,21,778, and **SILVER 04DEC2026 last traded at ₹1,54,205 per kg, up ₹6,392 or 4.32%** against ₹1,47,813. These are last-traded prices off MCX's own top-gainers board, stamped "As on 23 Nov 2026 - 23:55" — not exchange settlements, and no rupee change is derived from them for any other contract.

The reported reason: investors bought back oversold metal and pared bets on aggressive Federal Reserve tightening, with the Wall Street Journal attributing the turn in risk appetite to the reinstatement of Nvidia's chief executive, which lifted equities and other assets alongside the metals.

What comes next is Wednesday's US PCE inflation data. Markets were pricing a **93.4% probability of a 25 basis point Fed hike in December** at the time of Moneycontrol's Monday piece — a snapshot that moves through the day, quoted with its source and not adopted as a forecast here.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a 3.9% spot rebound eases the collateral arithmetic at the margin but does not reset it, because the Directions value gold on a 30-day average. One session does not repair an average that is still rolling over the lower prints of the past three weeks; the average is the number that governs the ceiling, not Monday's close.
Sources: [Morningstar (Dow Jones), gold settlement, 23 Nov](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611237211/comex-gold-settles-390-higher-at-364920-data-talk) · [Morningstar (Dow Jones), silver settlement, 23 Nov](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611237212/comex-silver-settles-515-higher-at-43147-data-talk) · [MCX top gainers, 23 Nov 23:55](https://www.mcxindia.com/market-data/top-gainers) · [Moneycontrol, 23 Nov](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/personal-finance/gold-and-silver-rebound-over-2-after-steep-weekly-losses-can-the-recovery-sustain-14086886.html)

### Markets are shut today; there is no 24 November close to report
The equity, equity-derivative, currency-derivative, SLB and interest-rate derivative segments are closed today, Tuesday 24 November, for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev. It is also a settlement holiday, so credits from Monday's trades may not be available. Trading resumes on Wednesday 25 November, with pre-open at 09:00 and the normal session 09:15–15:30.

MCX's commodity derivatives segment is closed for the morning session (09:00–17:00) but **trades in the evening session from 17:00 to 23:30/23:55**, including gold, silver and crude.

IBJA's own block reads "Holiday", so there is no 24 November rate and the domestic benchmark stays on Monday 23 November's PM session until Wednesday's AM session posts. AGLOC's block is dated 24 November and is covered below.

No index, stock, currency or bond figure dated 24 November appears in this edition, and any that did would be wrong.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly — but a holiday means no fresh domestic price discovery for a day, so the 30-day average that governs collateral valuation will carry Monday's print rather than a new one when the market reopens on Wednesday.

### Monday's close: banks fell three times as hard as NBFCs
The last session, Monday 23 November, was a sharp down day led by banks, and the gap between the two indices is the useful read. The **Nifty Bank fell 3.17% to 62,585.35** while the **Nifty NBFC fell 0.69% to 55,647.61** — about a fifth of the banks' decline. The Nifty 50 fell 1.75% to 25,349.65, Nifty PSU Bank 3.25% to 9,559.65, Nifty Private Bank 3.19% to 30,659.85 and Nifty Financial Services 2.49% to 28,153.50. India VIX rose 2.19% to 17.70.

The Sensex, which is a BSE index and does not appear in the NSE archive, **closed at 82,435.99, down 1,483.72 or 1.77%**, with a day's low of 82,395.88. The broader market held up better than the headline: Nifty Midcap 100 fell 1.01% and Nifty Smallcap 100 0.66%, with breadth at 1,179 advances against 2,455 declines on the NSE.

Among the gold-loan names, **Muthoot Finance closed at ₹2,543.30, down 0.28%**, and **IIFL Finance at ₹615.00, up 0.50%** — the two that held their ground. **Manappuram fell 3.39% to ₹271.00**, Muthoot Microfin 3.23% to ₹160.06 and Muthoot Capital 3.57% to ₹187.33. Shriram Finance was among the day's Nifty gainers at ₹995.90, up 2.46%. Bajaj Finance fell 2.36% to ₹1,095.50, Cholamandalam 2.33% to ₹1,831.00 and M&M Financial 0.50% to ₹286.85. **Muthoot Finance is not Muthoot Fincorp.**

Flows were supportive on the institutional side: FII/FPI were net buyers of **₹5,672.99 crore** and DIIs net sellers of **₹2,760.12 crore**, both NSE provisional. The **rupee closed at 92.91 to the dollar, down 23 paise or 0.25% from 92.68**, snapping a five-session winning streak, having touched 92.44 intraday — its strongest since April — and 93.11 at the low. The wires differ on this print to the paisa (Reuters puts the previous close at 92.67, and PTI's provisional figure is 92.92 at a different previous reference), so one is quoted here with its name rather than averaged across them. Brent settled at $91.94 a barrel, down 0.68%, and the dollar index was 103.69, down 0.05%.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the NBFC index's much smaller fall than the banks' is a comparison of two index moves, not evidence about any single lender, and Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no share price in it. Monday's rupee close matters more to the collateral arithmetic than the equity tape does.

### Today's AGLOC block is dated 24 November and carries Monday's close forward
AGLOC's block for 24 November puts the ceiling at **₹9,728 a gram at 85% LTV, ₹9,156 at 80% and ₹8,583 at 75%**, on a jewellery reference of **₹11,445**. Every band is up **₹72 to ₹82 a gram, or about 0.85%**, against the previous block — AGLOC's own 21–23 November row — of ₹9,646 / ₹9,078 / ₹8,511 on a reference of ₹11,348.

The reference is not a new quote. **₹11,445 a gram is exactly IBJA's 23 November PM 916 rate** (₹1,14,450 per 10 g ÷ 10), restated — which is what a holiday should produce, since there has been no session to move it. The three LTV bands cannot diverge from each other: each is a fixed percentage of the same single reference, so the identical 0.85% in every row is one move, not three.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these are the ceilings that apply today. A loan's permitted LTV is tested against a value that has risen 0.85% in a session but is still far below where the collateral stood when most of this year's book was written — which is the arithmetic in the next card.
Sources: [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA 23 Nov PM](https://ibjarates.com/)

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

### An EGM was held on 23 November; the proceedings were posted to the investor page this morning
Two new documents appeared on Muthoot Fincorp's investor page between Monday morning and Tuesday morning, and they are the only change: the **intimation of an extraordinary general meeting to be held on 23 November 2026**, and the **proceedings of that EGM, held on 23 November 2026**. The page grew from 2,768,430 bytes to 2,769,738 and from 871 distinct document names to 873, with nothing removed.

**What was resolved is not knowable from here, and this edition does not guess it.** The documents are served from a private bucket through presigned links that had already expired when the page was built, and unsigned requests are refused; the text cannot be read from this desk.

What is on the record is why a meeting was expected. The board meeting of 14 November — the same filing that carried the Q2 results — **recommended the conversion of 40,00,00,000 compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares**, and the reappointment of **Thomas John Muthoot, Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot for five years from 1 February 2027**. Both need shareholder approval. An EGM on 23 November is consistent with those two items being put to shareholders; it does not establish that they were passed, or that nothing else was on the agenda.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a completed CCCPS conversion would be a capital-structure event rather than new money raised, and its effect on the reported CRAR is not straightforward without the conversion terms. The proceedings document is the authority. Anyone relying on this should read it directly rather than take a summary from here.
Sources: [Muthoot Fincorp investor page](https://www.muthootfincorp.com/investors) · [BSE: Q2 FY27 Reg 52 filing and board recommendations, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)

### Q2 FY27 stands where it was filed: profit doubled, Stage III at 1.07%, CRAR 19.38%
Nothing in today's filings changes the quarter. The standing figures, each on its own date: **PAT of ₹779.41 crore for July–September 2026** against ₹388 crore a year earlier, **H1 PAT of ₹1,485 crore** on total income of ₹6,567 crore, quarterly total income of **₹3,408 crore, up 71% year-on-year**, **Stage III at 1.07%** against 1.41% a year earlier, net Stage III at 0.63% and **CRAR at 19.38%** — all from the Reg 52 filing of 14 November 2026.

On funding, the average cost of borrowing fell 121 basis points to **9.11% in FY26** from 10.32% in FY25, with overseas borrowings at 9.20% of total borrowings at March 2026, commercial paper at 8.92%, bank term loans at 39.69% of the mix, 67 listed NCD issuances, an average yield on loans of 21.38% against 22.47%, and NIM steady at 12.80%.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the Q2 numbers were struck on a book whose collateral was marked at September prices. Gold's move since then is not in them, which is the reason the next two quarters are the ones to watch rather than this one.
Sources: [Business Standard, 16 Nov 13:57 IST](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/quarterly-results/muthoot-fincorp-q2-profit-doubles-to-779-crore-on-better-asset-quality-126111601050_1.html) · [BSE: Q2 FY27 filing, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf) · [BusinessLine on borrowing costs, 12 Nov](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/muthoot-fincorp-diversifies-funding-to-trim-borrowing-cost/article71695055.ece)

### IPO status: SEBI's processing list still shows clarifications sought
The draft offer is with SEBI and has not moved. SEBI's draft-offer processing list, as on 20 November 2026, records the issue — lead manager Kotak Mahindra Capital, fresh issue only — with a **date of receipt of 13 August 2026**, under **clarifications sought, with the lead manager's response awaited**, and a last communication date of 12 November. No observations have been issued. There is no price band and no dates.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the offer is pending at the regulator, not at the company. Nothing in today's filings bears on it.

### What the 30-day-average rule does to a book after a 30% fall and a 3.9% bounce
The June 2025 Directions require collateral to be valued at the **lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day**, and the prescribed LTV to be maintained **throughout the tenor**. That combination is why the reported LTV breaches appear after a price fall rather than on the day of it: the average still carries the pre-fall prints while spot has already dropped, so the permitted loan value comes down gradually and a loan written at the old ceiling drifts above the current one without any new lending.

Worked on IBJA's own 916 series, and this is an illustration rather than any lender's book: 916 fell from **₹1,34,201 per 10 g on 17 November's PM session to ₹1,13,486 on 20 November's PM session**, a fall of **15.4%** in three sessions. A loan written at the 75% ceiling against the 17 November reference would sit at about **88.7%** of the 20 November reference on the same collateral — above the 85% ceiling that applies to any ticket size. The division is ₹1,34,201 ÷ ₹1,13,486 = 1.1825, and 75% × 1.1825 = 88.7%.

Monday's move runs the same arithmetic the other way but too slowly to matter yet: 916 at **₹1,14,450 on 23 November's PM session is up 0.85%** on 20 November, and Comex gold rose 3.90% on the day. One session does not repair a 30-day average that is still rolling over the past three weeks' lower prints. Two or three more sessions in the same direction would start to. **The 30-day average is the number to watch this week, not the spot print.**

What would change the picture, stated as conditions rather than predictions: a further fall in spot; the MPC's decision on 4 December; or any RBI communication that turns Monday's reported "greater scrutiny" into a written instruction. None of those has happened.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: this is the mechanism its book runs on, and it is direction-neutral — it dampens the damage from a fall and equally dampens the relief from a bounce. No Muthoot Fincorp book is described here.

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

### Three parallel securitisation amendments — and one of them binds Muthoot Fincorp
The RBI issued **three parallel securitisation amendments on 23 November**, one for each class of lender, all effective **1 April 2027**: the Small Finance Banks directions (RBI/2026-27/305, DOR.STR.REC.257/21-04-177/2026-27), the **Non-Banking Financial Companies directions (RBI/2026-27/306, DOR.STR.REC.258/21-04-177/2026-27)** and the All India Financial Institutions directions (RBI/2026-27/307, DOR.STR.REC.259/21-04-177/2026-27), the last signed by Vaibhav Chaturvedi, Chief General Manager.

In each, para 26 is substituted so that the issuance, holding and transfer of securitisation notes is **only in dematerialised form**, with a **minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore** at issuance and at every subsequent transfer; a new para 27A extends the requirement to notes issued before 1 April 2027. A proviso allows notes with amortisation structures to be traded at amortised value if the ticket falls below ₹1 crore.

**The NBFC one is the one that matters here.** It amends the NBFC Securitisation Transactions Directions, 2025, which govern the assignments and co-lending arrangements Muthoot Fincorp actually uses — the Q2 filing records ₹8,137.9 crore of direct assignment in the quarter and ₹3,583.8 crore of co-lending outstanding. The AIFI directions bind NABARD, NHB, SIDBI, EXIM Bank and NaBFID and do not bind the company; the SFB directions bind small finance banks. The National Housing Bank's presence at Monday's meeting is a separate fact and does not change any of these scopes.

SEBI issued nothing new: its circulars listing, re-fetched this morning, still has the **17 November 2026** circular on the commodity derivatives margin framework as its newest entry, with nothing dated 18 to 24 November.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: not a cost today, and not a change to LTV or credit rules. The dematerialised-notes and ₹1 crore ticket floor change the plumbing of any securitisation the company does or buys from 1 April 2027, which is a treasury and struct-ops item to diarise rather than a Q3 issue. The effect on its existing assignments is a question for the transaction documents, not for this edition.

## 🏘️ Sector Deep Dive — Tuesday: why a 15% fall in three sessions reads as a 100% LTV

### The lag is the story, and it runs both ways
The number that circulated on Monday — that certain cases are "breaching even 100 percent" LTV — is not a claim that lenders lent at 100%. It is what a constant-LTV rule produces when the collateral is marked on a trailing average and the price moves fast in one direction.

Take a book written near the January peak, when the 24-carat price was above ₹1.8 lakh per 10 g. A loan at 75% of collateral value then is at roughly 75% × (₹18,000 ÷ ₹12,495) ≈ 108% of the current 999 reference if nothing else changed — before any allowance for the 30-day average, which softens it slightly but does not rescue it. That cohort exists in the industry, and it is the cohort behind the reported breaches.

The other side of the same mechanism is the one to watch now. Because the average lags, a 3.9% bounce does not immediately restore lending headroom, and a further 5% fall does not immediately remove it. **The average, not the spot, sets the ceiling** — which means the next two weeks of prints matter more than any single session, and the 4 December MPC matters more than either, because it sets the cost of the funding that carries the book through the lag.

Crisil's read, published on 23 November, is that gold loans stay the fastest-growing NBFC segment at a roughly 40% CAGR over this fiscal and next after 78% growth last fiscal, that NBFC AUM reaches about ₹68 lakh crore by March 2028, and that a steep decline of more than 15% in gold prices is rare and unlikely to trigger a significant rise in credit costs. That is a rating agency's view of the sector and it is reported as such.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the vintage of its own book — how much was written in January and February near the peak — is the single number that determines whether this is a manageable tail or a provisioning event, and it is not in any public document.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Tuesday, 24 November 2026 (IST)

Tuesday edition for 24 November 2026 (IST), covering Monday 23 November to Tuesday morning; regulator pages read 07:03–07:35 IST; the exchanges are closed today for Guru Nanak Jayanti, so market figures elsewhere are Monday 23 November's closes.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

Three RBI instruments were issued on 23 November — parallel amendments to the small finance bank, NBFC and AIFI securitisation directions — and **one of them binds Muthoot Fincorp**: the Non-Banking Financial Companies (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026, effective 1 April 2027. Nothing else in the RBI, SEBI or IBBI lists changes a rule that applies to the company. The day's substantive regulatory event is not an instrument but a meeting: the RBI met the chief executives of select NBFCs, HFCs and microfinance institutions on Monday, and the official readout is now out, with reporting that it asked lenders for greater scrutiny of gold-loan LTVs. What was checked is set out below; the substance is the standing gold-loan rulebook, that meeting, and the next scheduled decision, the MPC on 2–4 December.

### The standing rulebook: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025
The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26), updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26); compliance was required by 1 April 2026, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted them stay under the earlier rules. Para 15 caps bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable under para 11; para 16 caps ornaments at 1 kg of gold (10 kg silver) and coins at 50 g gold (500 g silver) per borrower; para 17 values collateral at the lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day, per IBJA or a SEBI-regulated commodity exchange; para 19 sets maximum LTV at 85% (loans up to ₹2.5 lakh), 80% (₹2.5–5 lakh) and 75% (above ₹5 lakh); para 20 requires the prescribed LTV to be maintained on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor. LTV is computed on the amount repayable at maturity, including interest, for bullet-repayment loans — not merely the amount disbursed.

On auctions: para 37 requires adequate notice to the borrower or legal heir, and one month from the public notice where the borrower cannot be located; para 38 requires advertisements in at least two newspapers, one regional and one national; para 39 puts the auction through the lender's trained employee or an empanelled auctioneer; para 40 sets a reserve price not less than 90% of current value, 85% only after two failed auctions; para 41 requires the first auction physically in the lending branch's district, an adjoining district or online auction only if the first fails; para 42 bars the lender and related parties from bidding; para 43 requires the value fetched and dues adjusted to go to the borrower, any surplus refunded within seven working days of receiving the full proceeds.

Why this rulebook matters this week: every subject reported out of Monday's meeting sits on it. The continuous-LTV requirement in para 20, applied to collateral valued under para 17 at the lower of a 30-day average and the preceding day's close, is the mechanism that turns a price fall into reported LTV breaches with a lag — the average is still carrying pre-fall prints while spot has already dropped. Today's AGLOC ceiling is ₹9,728 a gram at the 85% band, up ₹82 from Monday's ₹9,646 but still far below where the collateral stood when most of this year's book was written. The industry's asks — a lower Tier-1 requirement, a revisit of the LTV rules and priority-sector inclusion — are representations; the industry has asked the RBI to review, and no instrument doing any of them appears in the sources checked.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these are the Directions its gold-loan book and auction practice run under; nothing in them changed today, and the reported scrutiny is a discussion, not an amendment.
Sources: [RBI: Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12859) · [RBI: (1st Amendment) Directions, 29 Sep 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12903) · [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/) · [Mint, 17 Nov 2026](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/gold-loan-nbfcs-seek-rbi-relief-on-capital-norms-as-new-rules-raise-npa-concerns-11794919898824.html)

### The new instruments, and who they actually bind: three parallel securitisation amendments
The RBI issued **three parallel securitisation amendments on 23 November 2026**, one for each class of lender, all effective **1 April 2027**:

| Instrument | Reference | Notification | Binds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small Finance Banks — Securitisation Transactions | RBI/2026-27/305, DOR.STR.REC.257/21-04-177/2026-27 | Id=13754 | Small finance banks |
| **Non-Banking Financial Companies — Securitisation Transactions** | **RBI/2026-27/306, DOR.STR.REC.258/21-04-177/2026-27** | **Id=13755** | **NBFCs, including Muthoot Fincorp** |
| All India Financial Institutions — Securitisation Transactions | RBI/2026-27/307, DOR.STR.REC.259/21-04-177/2026-27 | Id=13756 | NABARD, NHB, SIDBI, EXIM Bank, NaBFID |

In each, para 26 is substituted so that the issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes shall only be in **dematerialised form**, with a **minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore** at the time of issuance and at any subsequent transfer, and the originator must ensure its agreement with the special purpose entity requires arrangements with the registrar, depository and stock exchange to hold that floor. A proviso allows notes with amortisation structures to be traded at amortised value if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore. A new para 27A requires transactions in notes issued before 1 April 2027 to comply as well.

**Scope is the point, and it cuts the other way from a single instrument.** The NBFC amendment modifies the NBFC Securitisation Transactions Directions, 2025 — the framework under which Muthoot Fincorp runs its direct assignments and co-lending. Its Q2 FY27 filing records ₹8,137.9 crore of direct assignment in the quarter (1,65,596 accounts) and co-lending outstanding of ₹3,583.8 crore across ten arrangements. The AIFI directions bind only the all-India institutions, and the SFB directions bind small finance banks; neither reaches the company. The National Housing Bank's presence at Monday's meeting is a separate fact and does not change any of these scopes.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: no effect on LTV, credit or provisioning rules, and no cost today. From 1 April 2027 any securitisation note the company issues or holds must be dematerialised with a ₹1 crore minimum ticket — a treasury and struct-ops item to diarise, and a question for the transaction documents on existing deals rather than for this edition.
Sources: [RBI notification 13755, NBFC directions, 23 Nov 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13755&Mode=0) · [RBI notification 13756, AIFI directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13756&Mode=0) · [RBI notification 13754, SFB directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13754&Mode=0)

### The day's regulatory event: the RBI's NBFC/HFC meeting, and the gold-loan scrutiny reported out of it
The RBI met the managing directors and chief executives of select NBFCs, including government NBFCs, HFCs and microfinance institutions, in Mumbai on 23 November, per its own press release 2026-2027/1554 signed by Brij Raj, Chief General Manager. Representatives of Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC participated; all four Deputy Governors attended with other senior officers; the MD and CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated. The release itself records the Governor acknowledging the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting credit flow and is a readout, not an instrument — no rule changed. Reporting on the meeting adds that the RBI asked for greater scrutiny of gold loans as falling prices pressure LTVs (Economic Times ed. 24 Nov, 01:11 IST), that it has raised the frequency of portfolio reporting over the last 30–45 days (Moneycontrol, 23 Nov), and that NBFCs failing to reach a ₹10 crore net owned fund by March 2027 will get no further extension (ET). Those are reported, not gazetted: the net-owned-fund deadline already exists in the scale-based framework.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the scrutiny is sector-wide; its own Stage III is 1.07% at 30 September 2026, a lagging indicator against a fall that mostly happened after that date. No supervisory action against any named lender is reported.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1554](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64032) · [Economic Times, 24 Nov 01:11 IST](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/rbi-cautions-nbfcs-over-falling-gold-prices-and-rising-loan-to-value-ratios/articleshow/136113465.cms) · [Moneycontrol, 23 Nov 10:04 IST](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/commodities/rbi-steps-up-monitoring-of-gold-loan-portfolios-of-banks-nbfcs-as-ltv-concerns-emerge-14086885.html)

### The next scheduled decision: the MPC meets 2–4 December
The Monetary Policy Committee meets on 2–4 December 2026, with the decision due on **4 December**. The policy repo rate stands at **5.50%**, raised 25 basis points at the 5–7 October meeting, with the stance changed to calibrated tightening; SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%. October CPI inflation was **6.09%**, the first breach of the 6% upper tolerance band in two years, and economists expect a further 25 basis points in December with a terminal repo of 6.00–6.25%. ET reported on 23 November that the RBI is weighing a 25 or 50 basis point hike and that bankers raised gold-loan stress in the pre-policy consultations. This is inside the MPC's pre-policy quiet period, when no member comments publicly on the decision before it is announced.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the repo sets the floor under its cost of funds, and the last published average cost of borrowing was 9.11% for FY26. A 25 basis point hike is not itself the risk; the risk is the pass-through into bank term loans, which were 39.69% of the borrowing mix.
Sources: [RBI: October MPC resolution](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/bs_viewbulletin.aspx/BS_ViewBulletin.aspx?Id=24511) · [Business Standard, 13 Nov](https://www.business-standard.com/finance/news/rbi-repo-rate-6-percent-december-february-policy-inflation-october-126111300961_1.html) · [Business Standard, 16 Nov](https://www.business-standard.com/finance/news/economists-see-50-75-bps-more-rbi-rate-hikes-terminal-rate-at-6-6-25-126111601589_1.html) · [Economic Times, 23 Nov](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/banks-warn-higher-costs-could-hit-demand-as-rbi-weighs-further-repo-hike/articleshow/136082582.cms)

## What was checked

The RBI's press-release and notification listings, SEBI's circulars and legal-circulars listings and its draft-offer processing status, and IBBI's homepage were all re-fetched this morning (07:03–07:35 IST) and read to their date blocks: three RBI instruments appeared under the 23 November date block — the SFB, NBFC and AIFI securitisation amendments (Id=13754, 13755 and 13756), all effective 1 April 2027, of which the NBFC one governs Muthoot Fincorp's assignments and co-lending — while the RBI press-release block for 23 November carries the two meeting readouts (NBFC/HFC and urban co-operative banks), a Sovereign Gold Bond premature-redemption price for SGB 2021-22 Series I due 25 November, and routine liquidity operations including an overnight VRR auction on 25 November, none of which is a rule for a gold lender; the RBI notifications list has nothing later than the 11 November Domestic Money Transfer Directions apart from those three; SEBI's newest circular remains the 17 November review of the commodity derivatives margin framework, with nothing dated 18 to 24 November; SEBI's processing list still shows Muthoot Fincorp's draft offer under clarifications sought as on 20 November, with a date of receipt of 13 August 2026; and IBBI's footer reads "Last updated on: 16 Nov 2026", with no new insolvency instrument dated 24 November seen (the one 24 November hit on the page is a 2024 discussion paper).
Sources: [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [RBI notifications](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [RBI notification 13755, NBFC directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13755&Mode=0) · [RBI notification 13756, AIFI directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13756&Mode=0) · [RBI notification 13754, SFB directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13754&Mode=0) · [SEBI circulars listing](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0) · [SEBI draft offer processing](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/nov-2026/1795175784186.pdf) · [IBBI](https://ibbi.gov.in/)

cards.title: RBI presses NBFCs on gold-loan LTVs as collateral falls, ET reports
cards.summary: The Reserve Bank of India met the managing directors and chief executives of select NBFCs, including government NBFCs, housing finance companies and microfinance institutions, in Mumbai on Monday 23 November, and the official readout is now out. RBI press release 2026-2027/1554, dated 23 November and signed by Brij Raj, Chief General Manager, records that representatives of Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC also participated, that all four Deputy Governors — Shri Swaminathan J., Dr…
cards.impact: the reported scrutiny is sector-wide and no Muthoot Fincorp-specific detail appears in the sources checked. Its own last published asset-quality number is Stage III at 1.07% as at 30 September 2026, filed on 14 November, which is a lagging indicator against a price fall that mostly happened in October and November. The operative sentence for planning is the one about continuous LTV: the June 2025 Directions require the prescribed LTV to be maintained throughout the tenor,…

cards.title: Gold rebounds 3.9% on Comex — its biggest one-day gain since August
cards.summary: Comex front-month gold settled at $3,649.20 an ounce on Monday 23 November, up $136.90 or 3.90% — the largest one-day dollar gain since 5 August 2026, the largest one-day percentage gain since 3 February 2026, and enough to snap a three-session losing streak. It is 3.90% above the 52-week low of $3,512.30 set on Friday 20 November, and still down 15.64% year-to-date (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 23 Nov, 18:52 ET).
cards.impact: a 3.9% spot rebound eases the collateral arithmetic at the margin but does not reset it, because the Directions value gold on a 30-day average. One session does not repair an average that is still rolling over the lower prints of the past three weeks; the average is the number that governs the ceiling, not Monday's close.

cards.title: Markets are shut today; there is no 24 November close to report
cards.summary: The equity, equity-derivative, currency-derivative, SLB and interest-rate derivative segments are closed today, Tuesday 24 November, for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev. It is also a settlement holiday, so credits from Monday's trades may not be available.
cards.impact: none directly — but a holiday means no fresh domestic price discovery for a day, so the 30-day average that governs collateral valuation will carry Monday's print rather than a new one when the market reopens on Wednesday.

cards.title: Monday's close: banks fell three times as hard as NBFCs
cards.summary: The last session, Monday 23 November, was a sharp down day led by banks, and the gap between the two indices is the useful read. The Nifty Bank fell 3.17% to 62,585.35 while the Nifty NBFC fell 0.69% to 55,647.61 — about a fifth of the banks' decline.
cards.impact: the NBFC index's much smaller fall than the banks' is a comparison of two index moves, not evidence about any single lender, and Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no share price in it. Monday's rupee close matters more to the collateral arithmetic than the equity tape does.

cards.title: Today's AGLOC block is dated 24 November and carries Monday's close forward
cards.summary: AGLOC's block for 24 November puts the ceiling at ₹9,728 a gram at 85% LTV, ₹9,156 at 80% and ₹8,583 at 75% , on a jewellery reference of ₹11,445 . Every band is up ₹72 to ₹82 a gram, or about 0.85% , against the previous block — AGLOC's own 21–23 November row — of ₹9,646 / ₹9,078 / ₹8,511 on a reference of ₹11,348.
cards.impact: these are the ceilings that apply today. A loan's permitted LTV is tested against a value that has risen 0.85% in a session but is still far below where the collateral stood when most of this year's book was written — which is the arithmetic in the next card.

cards.title: An EGM was held on 23 November; the proceedings were posted to the investor page this morning
cards.summary: Two new documents appeared on Muthoot Fincorp's investor page between Monday morning and Tuesday morning, and they are the only change: the intimation of an extraordinary general meeting to be held on 23 November 2026 , and the proceedings of that EGM, held on 23 November 2026 . The page grew from 2,768,430 bytes to 2,769,738 and from 871 distinct document names to 873, with nothing removed.
cards.impact: a completed CCCPS conversion would be a capital-structure event rather than new money raised, and its effect on the reported CRAR is not straightforward without the conversion terms. The proceedings document is the authority. Anyone relying on this should read it directly rather than take a summary from here.

cards.title: Q2 FY27 stands where it was filed: profit doubled, Stage III at 1.07%, CRAR 19.38%
cards.summary: Nothing in today's filings changes the quarter. The standing figures, each on its own date: PAT of ₹779.41 crore for July–September 2026 against ₹388 crore a year earlier, H1 PAT of ₹1,485 crore on total income of ₹6,567 crore, quarterly total income of ₹3,408 crore, up 71% year-on-year , Stage III at 1.07% against 1.41% a year earlier, net Stage III at 0.63% and CRAR at 19.38% — all from the Reg 52 filing of 14 November 2026.
cards.impact: the Q2 numbers were struck on a book whose collateral was marked at September prices. Gold's move since then is not in them, which is the reason the next two quarters are the ones to watch rather than this one.

cards.title: IPO status: SEBI's processing list still shows clarifications sought
cards.summary: The draft offer is with SEBI and has not moved. SEBI's draft-offer processing list, as on 20 November 2026, records the issue — lead manager Kotak Mahindra Capital, fresh issue only — with a date of receipt of 13 August 2026 , under clarifications sought, with the lead manager's response awaited , and a last communication date of 12 November.
cards.impact: the offer is pending at the regulator, not at the company. Nothing in today's filings bears on it.

The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp LTV or loan-book figure for 24 November.

cards.title: What the 30-day-average rule does to a book after a 30% fall and a 3.9% bounce
cards.summary: The June 2025 Directions require collateral to be valued at the lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day , and the prescribed LTV to be maintained throughout the tenor . That combination is why the reported LTV breaches appear after a price fall rather than on the day of it: the average still carries the pre-fall prints while spot has already dropped, so the permitted loan value comes down…
cards.impact: this is the mechanism its book runs on, and it is direction-neutral — it dampens the damage from a fall and equally dampens the relief from a bounce. No Muthoot Fincorp book is described here.

cards.title: Three parallel securitisation amendments — and one of them binds Muthoot Fincorp
cards.summary: The RBI issued three parallel securitisation amendments on 23 November , one for each class of lender, all effective 1 April 2027 : the Small Finance Banks directions (RBI/2026-27/305, DOR.STR.REC.257/21-04-177/2026-27), the Non-Banking Financial Companies directions (RBI/2026-27/306, DOR.STR.REC.258/21-04-177/2026-27) and the All India Financial Institutions directions (RBI/2026-27/307, DOR.STR.REC.259/21-04-177/2026-27), the last signed by Vaibhav Chaturvedi, Chief…
cards.impact: not a cost today, and not a change to LTV or credit rules. The dematerialised-notes and ₹1 crore ticket floor change the plumbing of any securitisation the company does or buys from 1 April 2027, which is a treasury and struct-ops item to diarise rather than a Q3 issue. The effect on its existing assignments is a question for the transaction documents, not for this edition.

cards.section: Sector Deep Dive — Tuesday: why a 15% fall in three sessions reads as a 100% LTV
cards.title: The lag is the story, and it runs both ways
cards.summary: The number that circulated on Monday — that certain cases are "breaching even 100 percent" LTV — is not a claim that lenders lent at 100%. It is what a constant-LTV rule produces when the collateral is marked on a trailing average and the price moves fast in one direction.
cards.impact: the vintage of its own book — how much was written in January and February near the peak — is the single number that determines whether this is a manageable tail or a provisioning event, and it is not in any public document.

cards.title: The standing rulebook: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025
cards.summary: The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26), updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26); compliance was required by 1 April 2026, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted them stay under the earlier rules. Para 15 caps bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable under para 11; para 16 caps ornaments at 1 kg of gold (10 kg silver) and coins…
cards.impact: these are the Directions its gold-loan book and auction practice run under; nothing in them changed today, and the reported scrutiny is a discussion, not an amendment.
